chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: Billy Taylor and bassist Joe Benjamin; the Gramercy Five
summary: Collins loves working with Billy Taylor, and Taylor, Joe Benjamin, Charlie Smith and Collins briefly formed Artie Shaw's Gramercy Five.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Of course I worked with him whenever he came out here to California with the big band. What was it, the David Frost Show? I would always do the show with him out here. And very fond of him, he's a marvelous person, very intelligent and musically and otherwise. And a gentleman, you know. It's always a pleasure working with him.

But I did quite a bit of recording with him. And I at one time had a marvelous bass player that worked with us by the name of Joe Benjamin, and I liked Joe very much because aside from his playing he was a wonderful person. And Joe also worked with -- opposite us with Sarah Vaughan's group. You know, he played with Sarah for quite a while. But what I want to tell you, for a fleeting moment we all were part of the Gramercy Five. Joe, Benjamin, Charlie Smith, Billy Taylor and myself. We worked for Artie Shaw. That was -- when was that, let me see. That was around '47, '48, around this time. Of course at this time Artie was going through this thing with Joe McCarthy.
